title: Canary probes and watermarking for embed+rerank quality
creator: Priya Desai
description: Design and implement a lightweight canary probing harness and watermark-based drift detectors to catch embedding + reranker quality regressions caused by config or model changes. The harness must run automatically when model variants, quantization profiles, or reranker hyperparameters are modified, and produce an actionable scorecard (recall/precision deltas, per-query regressions, drift metrics) before changes are rolled out. Goal: catch quality regressions earlier than full shadow-eval runs and avoid human-in-the-loop delays.
outcome_goal: Provide automated pre-rollout gating with < 24h feedback, reduce post-deploy embedding/reranker regressions by 60% vs baseline, and generate scorecards that map to rollout decisions (accept, require manual review, block).
acceptance_criteria: Canary harness triggers on model/config change events in CI and Console change API
Generates a scorecard with baseline vs candidate: recall@1/5/10, precision@k, average MRR, and per-query delta list
Implements a watermarking metric for embedding population shift (cosine distribution drift + Wasserstein on pairwise similarities)
Automated decision rules: PASS (delta within thresholds), REVIEW (outliers present but no global fail), FAIL (stat sig degradation or drift > threshold)
Integrates with evals dashboard and sends alerts to #infra-evals when FAIL
End-to-end run completes within budgeted compute (<= 2 GPU-hours per full canary run for 100k probe queries)
design_notes: Probing dataset: curated synthetic + customer-like queries (10k-100k) sampled by workload buckets (short / long / multi-turn / domain-specific)
Two-tier evaluation: lightweight canary (fast, lower sample) vs bulk shadow-eval (deep, scheduled)
Use stratified sampling to preserve distribution of sequence lengths and token budgets so batching behavior stays representative
Scorecard components: aggregate metrics, cohort breakouts, per-query top-N difference heatmap, embedding drift summaries

Drift detection: compare cosine similarity histograms (candidate vs baseline) and compute Wasserstein distance; also compute embedding centroid shift and a tail-regression indicator for top-k nearest neighbor changes
Significance testing: bootstrap confidence intervals for recall/precision deltas and Holm–Bonferroni correction when evaluating multiple cohorts
Trade-offs: heavier statistical tests increase run time; we bias canary for precision on false-positive reduction (avoid blocking safe changes) while surfacing risky regressions for manual review
implementation_plan: Step 1: Build probe runner and dataset selector (Evan) - implement sampling hooks and synthetic query generator
Step 2: Instrument embedding distribution collectors in runtime (lightweight histogram export) - infra/serving changes
Step 3: Implement scorecard generator service (stat tests, drift metrics) and CLI integration with CI
Step 4: Add automated decision rules and map results to Console rollout API (can block canary/auto-fallback)
Step 5: Wire alerts and dashboards (Grafana + Console evals tab), create runbook for REVIEW outcomes
Step 6: Run baseline calibration across 10 representative customers and tune thresholds
test_plan: Unit tests for sampling and metric calculations
Integration test: simulated model swap in staging triggers canary run and produces scorecard
Regression test: inject synthetic degradation (noise in embeddings) and assert FAIL path triggers
Performance test: end-to-end canary completes under compute budget for 100k probes
A/B validation: compare canary verdicts vs full shadow-eval on 20 historical config changes to measure FP/FN rates
monitoring_and_alerts: Primary alert: canary-run FAIL -> Pager to on-call infra-evals and message in #infra-evals
Triage dashboard: recent canary runs, pass/review/fail rates, mean delta trends, and embedding drift time-series
SLO: 95% of canary runs complete within 24h of trigger; alert if falling below
Automated ticket creation: failed canaries open a ticket with attached scorecard and top-20 regressed queries
rollout_plan: Start: Opt-in for canary gating on non-critical model variants for two weeks
Phase 1: Enforce REVIEW for changes where canary shows localized regressions (manual QA required)
Phase 2: Auto-block FAIL outcomes and require rollback or mitigation run
Phase 3: Expand gating to higher-traffic variants and tie into Dedicated/Private release pipelines
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy probes produce false positives. Mitigation: increase sample size for cohorts with high variance and require multiple run confirmations before BLOCKing
Risk: compute cost for frequent canaries. Mitigation: adaptive sampling frequency and sample size based on magnitude of change and historical volatility
Risk: drift signal doesn't correlate to user-visible impact. Mitigation: run targeted A/B checks for a small customer subset before enforcing blocks
open_questions: What default thresholds for Wasserstein/cosine drift should we adopt for 'FAIL' vs 'REVIEW'?
Should canary runs be triggered only on model/config changes or also by periodic schedule to detect silent drift?
How do we surface the per-query examples in Console without leaking PII for customer-derived probes? Need redaction policy
